papers.title: Mechanical Behaviour of Additively Manufactured Ti-6Al-4V Dumbbell Lattice Structures: Insights From Compression and Fatigue Analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract Lattice structures exhibit mechanical behavior that plays a vital role in their applications across industries such as aerospace and biomedical engineering. This study focuses on understanding the compression and fatigue behaviour of these structures through a combination of experimental testing and finite element analysis (FEA). Specimens are fabricated using laser powder bed fusion, ensuring high precision in geometry and material properties. Quasi-static compression tests reveal the deformation mechanisms and failure patterns, characterized by layer-by-layer collapse and strut failures localized at the mid-sections. For computational analysis, Abaqus is used to perform static simulations, evaluating stress distribution, load-bearing capacity, and deformation under compressive loads. The results from the static analysis serve as inputs for fatigue life predictions in Fe-safe, enabling the assessment of cyclic performance and durability. This integrated approach bridges the gap between static mechanical behaviour and dynamic fatigue response, offering comprehensive insights into the structural performance of lattice designs. A comparative analysis of experimental results and computational predictions highlights a strong correlation in terms of stress-strain behaviour, deformation modes, and failure localization. The study emphasizes the role of geometry, relative density, and nodal reinforcement in influencing mechanical performance. These findings underscore the reliability of FEA for predicting real-world behavior and guide the optimization of lattice structures for enhanced compression strength and fatigue resistance. By combining experimental and computational methods, this research provides a robust framework for designing lattice structures tailored to demanding mechanical requirements. The outcomes are particularly relevant for applications requiring lightweight, high-strength components with superior fatigue life, paving the way for advancements in additive manufacturing and structural design.

papers.title: Life Cycle Assessment to Achieve Sustainability in Pre- and Post-Processing: WAAM Vs. Wrought Ti-6Al-4V
papers.abstract: Abstract The shift toward sustainable manufacturing has intensified the necessity for examining the ecological impact of different production methods. This article conducts a cradle-to-gate Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) of ‘conventional wrought processing’ and ‘Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing’ (WAAM) for Ti-6Al-4V alloy, followed by post-processing under cryogenic (LCO2) cutting conditions. The environmental impact assessment covers key indicators, including climate change potential, resource depletion, terrestrial ecotoxicity, and human toxicity. The results reveal that WAAM exhibits a significantly higher environmental burden, with 261% greater terrestrial ecotoxicity, 32% higher climate change impact, and 104% more metal resource depletion compared to wrought Ti-6Al-4V. Additionally, WAAM consumes 25% more fossil-based energy and 44% more water, highlighting its higher resource intensity. The human toxicity assessment indicates that WAAM results in 36% greater carcinogenic toxicity and 19% higher non-carcinogenic toxicity, largely attributed to increased emissions from titanium extraction and tungsten carbide tool production for post-processing. While WAAM offers a reduction in material waste through near-net-shape manufacturing, this benefit is offset by its excessive energy consumption and emissions. The power consumption during drilling is nearly identical for both processing routes, reinforcing that pre-machining (raw material) factors dominate environmental impact, while tool wear in WAAM is twice as high, leading to increased resource consumption. These findings emphasize the need for process optimization to further improve the sustainability of titanium alloy manufacturing.

papers.title: Study of Laser Shock Peening Impact on the Wettability of Ti-Grade 23 Alloy
papers.abstract: Abstract Titanium and its alloys are extensively used in critical applications due to their exceptional strength-to-weight ratio, corrosion resistance, and biocompatibility. Among these, Ti Grade 23 (Ti-6Al-4V ELI) is particularly valued for its improved ductility, superior fatigue strength, and reduced interstitial elements. This study investigates the effect of Laser Shock Peening (LSP) on the wetting characteristics of Ti Grade 23 alloy, a property essential for enhancing biocompatibility and tribological performance in biomedical and industrial applications. LSP uses a nanosecond laser to impart compressive residual stresses into the alloy’s surface. These stresses lead to surface chemistry, microstructure, and surface energy alterations, collectively influencing wettability. Experiments were conducted by systematically varying two key parameters, the number of laser passes (P) and the water level (L), to explore their combined effect on the alloy’s wettability. The experimental findings reveal a significant transformation in surface wettability, with the contact angle increasing from hydrophilic (65°) to hydrophobic (90°). This transition is attributed to induced compressive stress, surface topography modifications, and crystal structure changes due to the LSP process. The observed wettability alterations suggest that LSP is a viable method for tailoring surface characteristics to meet the requirements of advanced engineering and biomedical applications. This study underscores the potential of LSP as a robust and versatile surface modification technique for Ti Grade 23. The results contribute to the broader understanding of how laser processing parameters influence surface properties, enabling the development of next-generation materials for critical applications.

papers.title: Evaluation of Grain Size and Improvement of Residual Stresses Through the Heat Treatment in Ti-6Al-4V Alloy Using Electron Beam Welding
papers.abstract: Abstract Electron beam welding (EBW) was employed to join Ti-6Al-4V alloy in this study. Ti-6Al-4V is highly reactive in an open atmosphere, making it very difficult to weld. Hence, EBW is the preferred option to join the Ti-6Al-4V alloy as it is carried out under vacuum conditions. The aim of this study is to evaluate the grain size and residual stresses induced during the EBW in the butt joints through electron back-scattered diffraction (EBSD) and residual stress analysis. Consequently, the microstructural analysis revealed the fine acicular α′ martensite, Widmanstätten α, with transformed β structure in the fusion zone. EBSD analysis confirmed the fine-grain distribution, with an average size of 1.30 μm to 1.33 μm after welding, which produced a promising welding strength. Subsequently, the residual stress entrapment was largely mitigated after employing post-weld heat treatment (PWHT) in the weldment. Finally, the residual stress results were compared with those of as-welded and heat-treated ones. The results of the EBSD and residual stress analysis confirmed remarkable findings regarding Ti-6Al-4V welding. From these findings, it can be concluded that EBW with PWHT was highly recommended for the welding of Ti-6Al-4V alloy.

papers.title: Fabrication of Bio-Inspired Surface Texturing of Ti-6Al-4V ELI by Laser Induced Technique to Improve Wear Resistance and Controlled Wettability for Biomedical Application
papers.abstract: Abstract Surface textures with different shapes/sizes and characteristics are gaining worldwide popularity due to their broader applications. Among them, controlled wettability for different materials through surface textures are essential to reduce adhesion of bacteria, bacterial contamination and growth, drug delivery, single point cutting tool and aerospace application. Even though, identification and preparation efficiency of favorable bio-inspired surface texture with optimum laser input parameters are comparatively complex from normal textures through any material processing methods due to their complexity of their shapes/size, form accuracy, dimensions and aspect ratio. Hence, this study focuses on creating different types of surface texture like oblique textured at different scanning angles (0°, 0°/90°, 0°/30°,and 0°/45°) on biomaterial surface Ti-6Al-4V ELI for controlling the wettability. The machining of Ti-6Al-4V ELI using ultra-short pulse laser were set input parameters such as out power ranging from 5W, no. of repetition three, wavelength of 1030 nm, scanning speed range 100 mm/s, temporal width of 350 fs and for all the texture types. The result of the wettability test indicates that Ti-6Al-4V ELI is hydrophilic without texture. After texture, it varies from hydrophilic to hydrophobic depending on the texture type and laser parameter.

papers.title: Real-Time Analysis of Surface Roughness During Micro-Turning of Ti-6Al-4V Alloys Using Vision-Based Techniques
papers.abstract: Abstract Surface roughness is an important characteristic that influences the quality and performance of precision-engineered components, especially in micro-turning applications. This study investigates a machine vision-based technique for accurately assessing the surface roughness of Ti-6Al-4V alloy. A high-resolution optical imaging system is integrated with a micro-turning setup to acquire surface photographs of machined components. The focused area of the images is cropped, stitched and enhanced, before being employed with Gray-Level Cooccurrence Matrix (GLCM) texture analysis to extract important features: contrast, correlation, energy, homogeneity, and entropy. These characteristics are correlated to surface roughness values acquired using a contact profilometer. Robust machine learning models: Random Forest Regressor (RFR), Radial Basis Function Neural Network (RBFNN), Support Vector Regressor (SVR), and XGBoost are trained to predict surface roughness based on these features. Among the trained machine learning models SVR performed best in prediction, with a Mean Square Error (MSE) of 0.032 and R2 score of 0.84, whereas RFR and RBFNN exhibit moderate performance. Whereas XGBoost’s performance is poor as compared to other models. The results demonstrate the feasibility of near real-time in-situ, non-contact surface roughness measurement with improved accuracy compared to conventional methods.

papers.title: Improving Adhesion Strength of Diamond-Like Carbon Coating on Ti6Al4V Through Substrate Roughness Analysis
papers.abstract: Abstract This study focuses on enhancing the adhesion of Diamond-Like Carbon (DLC) coating on Ti6Al4V substrate by surface roughness analysis and incorporating a titanium (Ti) interlayer. Two types of Ti6Al4V substrates, viz., polished and rough, were prepared with surface roughness values of approximately 50 nm and 3.5 μm, respectively. A Ti interlayer was deposited using chemical vapor deposition (CVD) prior to the application of the DLC coating, which was carried out using plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD), with the aim of investigating how surface texture and the presence of an interlayer influence DLC coating adhesion. Advanced material characterization techniques were employed to support the study, including nanoindentation and wear testing for mechanical property evaluation. The chemical structure of the DLC film was analyzed using Raman spectroscopy. Additional analyses included Optical Profiler for surface topography, and contact angle measurements to evaluate wetting properties were carried out. Optimal adhesion was observed at a surface roughness of 3.5 μm. Use of Ti interlayer coatings further enhances the adhesion. The findings emphasize the importance of moderated surface roughness and interlayer coatings in enhancing the tribological properties of Ti-6Al-4V substrates, making DLC coatings a viable solution for demanding applications in aerospace, biomedical, and other industries

summary_en.result: Optimal adhesion was achieved at a surface roughness of 3.5 μm, and the Ti interlayer further enhanced coating adhesion.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing (nanoindentation and wear testing) and Raman spectroscopy were used to characterize the coated samples.
